rows.title: Opinion: Campaigns Are Rewarded For Winning, Not Being Cost-Effective
rows.standfirst: NPR's Scott Simon reflects on the record amount of money spent this campaign season, a goodly amount spent by candidates who did not win.

rows.title: 'Secret Life Of Groceries' Shines A Light On Bounty's Dark Side
rows.standfirst: Keeping U.S. markets filled with a dazzling array of choices relies on an army of farmers, suppliers, truckers and retail workers. What's gained and lost as all that food makes its way to the shelves?

rows.title: With Trump's Loss, Murdoch's Fox News Faces Wrath And Tough Choices
rows.standfirst: Rupert Murdoch struck an alliance with President Trump early on, and Fox News has bolstered his presidency. With Joe Biden's victory, Fox is stepping warily to avoid alienating Trump supporters.

rows.title: Jobs Friday: Not Bad, Not Not Bad
rows.standfirst: The US economy added more than 600,000 jobs in October. Team Indicator assembles the Jobs Friday Ninja squad to get their take.

rows.title: Hacking The Perfect Auction
rows.standfirst: A Nobel-Prize winner spent years designing an auction to sell off the airwaves, which are owned by the public. But Wall Street found a tiny flaw. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Stocks Post Best Week Since April Despite Tumultuous And Unresolved Election
rows.standfirst: Investors are betting on at least two more years of divided government, spurring the best weekly stock gains in months.

rows.title: What Blockbuster Automaker Profits Tell Us About The Pandemic Economy
rows.standfirst: The auto industry was devastated this spring by coronavirus shutdowns. But the recovery has been much faster and stronger than anyone anticipated as demand for new trucks and SUVs continues.

rows.title: Alcohol Delivery Company Drizly Sees Sales Jump Amid Election Wait
rows.standfirst: Americans found comfort in wine, liquor and beer while awaiting the election results, according to an online delivery company. Its Election Day sales were up about 68% compared with recent Tuesdays.

rows.title: Federal Supply Deal For COVID-19 Antibody Treatment Lacks Some Customary Protections
rows.standfirst: To boost the supply of Regeneron's antibody therapy for COVID-19, the federal government entered into a $450 million supply contract. Details of the deal show some safeguards are missing.

rows.title: 'An Era Is Coming To An End': Travelers Bid Fond Farewell To Berlin's Tegel Airport
rows.standfirst: The airport opened in 1948 and is closing as Berlin's new international hub opens after a series of delays. Although COVID-19 has hampered travel, Germans are visiting Tegel to relive old memories.

rows.title: Unemployment Drops To 6.9%, But Pandemic Surge Clouds Recovery
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 638,000 jobs last month as the unemployment rate dipped to 6.9%. A winter spike in coronavirus infections threatens to further weaken job growth.

rows.title: Auto Sales Rebound Faster Than Analysts Had Predicted
rows.standfirst: Earlier this year things were looking grim for the auto sector. Plants were shut down and experts predicted a big drop in demand. But now automakers are making a lot of money.

rows.title: Pandemic Expedites ESPN Employee Purge, Hundreds Laid Off
rows.standfirst: ESPN informs employees that 300 individuals will be let go and another 200 positions will remain unfilled, shedding 10% of its workforce.

rows.title: When Life Gives You Lemons...Start The Mafia?
rows.standfirst: The essential ingredient in the birth of the mafia as we know it wasn't the threats or the murders or the other stuff that's great for Hollywood. It was...lemons.

rows.title: Wall Street Bet On A 'Blue Wave,' But Divided Government Suits It Just Fine Too
rows.standfirst: Stocks have traditionally done well with a Democrat in the White House and Congress under Republican control.

rows.title: Conservatives Flock To Mercer-Funded Parler, Claim Censorship On Facebook And Twitter
rows.standfirst: Backed by Rebekah Mercer, Parler is now one of the most downloaded smartphone apps, as conservatives complaining of censorship by Facebook and Twitter seek out other social media alternatives.

rows.title: Analysis: Is Trump's Next Foe Fox News?
rows.standfirst: Since Election Day, President Trump has attacked Fox News repeatedly, particularly its newsroom. Now comes chatter from Washington that he wants to start up his own media outfit to take on Fox.

rows.title: Biden Time
rows.standfirst: Four things Joe Biden can do as president — even if the Democrats don't control Congress. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Turkey Business
rows.standfirst: COVID-19-related travel and get-together restrictions are impacting small businesses across the U.S. this holiday season. The Indicator talks to a turkey farmer about how the pandemic has affected business this year.

rows.title: Trump's TikTok Sell-By Date Extended By 15 Days
rows.standfirst: The reprieve in the latest sigh of relief for the massively popular video app, but uncertainty hangs over its future.

rows.title: Elon Musk Tests Positive And Negative For Coronavirus, Awaiting Confirmation
rows.standfirst: Musk was using the less-accurate rapid antigen tests. He said something "bogus" was happening and is waiting results from a test that is considered more reliable but takes longer to process.

rows.title: Vaccine Could Unlock Trillions In Spending, Leading To 'Biden Boom'
rows.standfirst: Pent-up demand from households that have been cooped up over the last eight months could drive a spending boom in the spring, providing a big boost to the economy.

rows.title: Ant's IPO Woes
rows.standfirst: Ant Group is a fintech firm that was set to launch with the world's largest ever IPO. But just before its shares started trading, Chinese regulators pulled the plug. NPR's Emily Feng explains why.

rows.title: Twitter Says Steps To Curb Election Misinformation Worked
rows.standfirst: Ahead of Election Day, the social network put in place several measures to fight the spread of false claims. On Thursday it shared data showing some of its changes were effective.

rows.title: Twitter Keeps Some Measures It Says Slowed Election Misinformation
rows.standfirst: The social network says it will keep some changes that were effective in slowing down the spread of false claims about the election.

rows.title: Playstation 5, Xbox Series X Bring Sony-Microsoft Rivalry To A New Generation
rows.standfirst: New video game consoles from Microsoft and Sony are out this week — the latest installment in a long-running battle between two companies competing for dominance in the video game market.

rows.title: 'I Come Up Short Every Day': Couples Under Strain As Families Are Stuck At Home
rows.standfirst: Couples are struggling to redefine their own roles as they look to navigate a pandemic that has upended many aspects of domestic life.

rows.title: Pfizer CEO Sold Millions In Stock After Coronavirus Vaccine News, Raising Questions
rows.standfirst: Pfizer's CEO sold $5.6 million worth of stock on Monday. The company says the stock sale was made as part of a preset plan. But NPR found irregularities about when the CEO entered into that plan.

rows.title: Let Them Grow Beards: UPS Relaxes Rules On Drivers' Facial Hair
rows.standfirst: After years of strict rules surrounding its workers' personal appearance, UPS is loosening up. The company said it wanted to make employees "feel comfortable, genuine and authentic."

rows.title: The Lessons Of Pets.com
rows.standfirst: The tech bubble of the 90s was a time when companies with weak business models and flashy advertising secured massive investments. This is the story of perhaps the most infamous case study: Pets.com.

rows.title: Trump Appointee Unconstitutionally Interfered With VOA, Judge Rules
rows.standfirst: A federal judge ordered the CEO over the Voice of America to stop investigating its journalists for anti-Trump bias, saying he caused "self-censorship and the chilling of First Amendment expression."

rows.title: All Your Genes Are Belong To Us
rows.standfirst: Who owns your genes, anyway? For a while, Big Biotech patented 20% of the human genome. Then a lawyer took them to the Supreme Court. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Voice of America's 5 Months Under Trump CEO: Lawsuits, Bias Claims, And A Sex Scandal
rows.standfirst: Michael Pack is nearing the close of his turbulent tenure as CEO of the parent agency to the Voice of America. After firings and claims of bias, staffers say they fear more damage on his way out.

rows.title: Forum: Race For The COVID-19 Vaccine
rows.standfirst: Watch an expert panel discussion on the effort to develop and deploy safe and effective vaccines against COVID-19 on Friday, Nov. 20, to be live-streamed here at 12 p.m. ET

rows.title: Pfizer Asks FDA To Approve Its COVID-19 Vaccine For Emergency Use
rows.standfirst: The pharmaceutical giant and partner BioNTech announced Friday that they are submitting a formal request to the Food and Drug Administration, just days after the vaccine was shown to be 95% effective.

rows.title: Lawsuit Reveals Tyson Managers Took Bets On How Many Workers Would Get COVID-19
rows.standfirst: NPR's Rachel Martin talks with Clark Kauffman of the Iowa Capital Dispatch about a lawsuit involving Tyson Foods supervisors betting money on the number of workers who would contract COVID-19.

rows.title: Tyson Managers Suspended After Allegedly Betting If Workers Would Contract COVID
rows.standfirst: The move comes a day after the family of a deceased employee sued Tyson, claiming "incorrigible, willful and wanton disregard for worker safety at its pork processing facility in Waterloo, Iowa."

rows.title: Make Trade Stale Again
rows.standfirst: President-elect Joe Biden's inauguration will have massive implications for trade policy. Soumaya Keynes explains how Biden's approach to trade might differ from Trump's.

rows.title: Use It Or Lose It: Parents Set Wages Aside For Child Care. Now It's At Risk
rows.standfirst: For many families, 2020 ended up being a year with fewer child-care expenses. Now parents with unspent funds in their dependent-care flexible spending accounts are trying to figure out what to do.

rows.title: Pfizer CEO On Next Steps For Coronavirus Vaccine And His Controversial Stock Trade
rows.standfirst: Albert Bourla, head of the pharmaceutical giant, discusses plans for distributing its vaccine, which it says is 95% effective, and explains the timing of his $5.6 mllion sale of Pfizer stock.

rows.title: 'We Need To Build More Homes': Prices Soar Amid Housing Shortage
rows.standfirst: It's not only low interest rates pushing up prices to record highs. A historic lack of homes for sale is a big part of it too. And it's making homeownership unaffordable for too many people.

rows.title: Facebook Says It's Doing A Better Job Of Catching Hate Speech Before Users See It
rows.standfirst: The social network says hate speech accounts for a tiny fraction of the posts people see. It's relying on automated systems to catch it, but is under pressure to do better.

rows.title: 12 Million To Lose Jobless Benefits The Day After Christmas Unless Congress Acts
rows.standfirst: If Congress doesn't compromise and pass another relief bill, a new study finds a staggering number of Americans will lose a critical financial lifeline as the pandemic worsens.

rows.title: Florida Looks At A Winter Without Canadians
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus pandemic continues to rip across the U.S. killing many and infecting hundreds of thousands of people each week. It's also upending part-time residencies between Florida and Canada.

rows.title: Climate Activists Want Biden To Bar Appointees With Fossil Fuel Ties
rows.standfirst: Climate activists say Biden's staff picks are a sign of his seriousness about tackling the issue. But banning anyone with fossil fuel ties could wipe out a lot of experience in getting things done.

rows.title: Electric Car Chargers: When Supply Drives Demand
rows.standfirst: People are hesitant to buy electric cars because fast chargers still aren't widely available. The irony? Most people charge at home, not with fast chargers. NPR's Camila Domonoske explains.

rows.title: U.S. Shoppers Might Spend $13 Million Per Minute During Cyber Monday Peak
rows.standfirst: Despite the pandemic recession, holiday sales are expected to set a new record, topping $755 billion.

rows.title: More Americans Pay Rent On Credit Cards As Lawmakers Fail To Pass Relief Bill
rows.standfirst: Many Americans who've lost income in the pandemic are falling deeper into debt — forced to pay bills or even their rent on credit cards. It's a sign of trouble ahead for the economy.

rows.title: Newsmax Rises On Wave Of Resentment Toward Media — Especially Fox News
rows.standfirst: Conservative Newsmax TV has enjoyed a sharp burst in ratings as President Trump has urged his fans to turn away from Fox News.

rows.title: IRS Says Its Own Error Sent $1,200 Stimulus Checks To Non-Americans Overseas
rows.standfirst: The IRS now says its own error caused thousands of non-Americans living overseas to mistakenly receive $1,200 stimulus checks — and the mistake could happen again if more stimulus money goes out.

rows.title: Virtual Charter Schools Are Booming, Despite A Checkered Reputation
rows.standfirst: For-profit virtual charter schools have been dogged by complaints of low student performance, fraud and waste. Still, many are seeing a pandemic-induced enrollment surge.

rows.title: A Black Friday With Masked Shoppers And Booming Online Sales
rows.standfirst: Shoppers encountered temperature checks and mall Santas behind plexiglas shields. But online sales may have stolen the show.

rows.title: What's The Story? Narratives And The Economy
rows.standfirst: The great toilet paper shortage of 2020 wasn't caused by the virus or by a disruption to manufacturing. It was caused by a story: one that we told ourselves. On the Indicator: how stories can affect the economy.

rows.title: Hot Dog Hail Mary (Classic)
rows.standfirst: The Falcons are trying something radical: Making their food cheaper. It could break stadium economics.

rows.title: 6 U.S. Citgo Executives Convicted And Sentenced In Venezuela
rows.standfirst: First arrested in Venezuela in November 2017, they were convicted Thanksgiving Day on corruption charges and immediately sentenced to more than eight years in prison.

rows.title: Restaurants Reinvent Themselves For Thanksgiving And Beyond: 'You Just Pivot'
rows.standfirst: A Japanese café sells plants and green-tea pie. An Italian restaurant caters a prime-rib dinner. A steak-and-fries chain delivers free meals for the elderly. "Fight or flight," one manager says.

rows.title: James Wolfensohn, Former World Bank Chief And Champion Of The Poor, Dies At 86
rows.standfirst: The financier is credited with transforming the World Bank. Among his reforms, he is said to have given "voice to the poor and magnify the impact of development investments."

rows.title: Swamp Gravy (UPDATE)
rows.standfirst: Colquitt, Georgia, was struggling. And then musical theater came along. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Thanksgiving Dinner Is The Cheapest In 35 Years
rows.standfirst: Each year, the American Farm Bureau estimates the cost of Thanksgiving dinner. The main finding this year? Thanksgiving dinner is the cheapest it's been since the survey started 35 years ago.

rows.title: 'It Is Slightly Terrifying.' New Orleans Chef Braces For A Bittersweet Thanksgiving
rows.standfirst: Like many small business owners, Kelly Fields is walking a fine line between keeping her restaurant open and her employees safe. As much as she's staying vigilant, she's wary of another shutdown.
